the spatial patterns of T.nucifera trees are determined by complex interactions between adaptive processes and stochastic processes in extremely heterogeneous Gotjwal terrain.
spatial patterns of old-grown T. nuciferas are complexly determined by the interactions of adaptive, stochastic, and historical processes.
spatial patterns of the Torreya forest in Jeju Island were determined by complex interactions among sex and size, microhabitats, and survival and mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spatial structure of T. nuficera trees in this old-grown forest is a result of a complex interplay of sex, size, microhabitat, and stochastic processes.

sex-related differences in spatial distribution patterns of T. nucifera trees in the old-growth forest are likely to be influenced by size, and the Gotjawal terrain, rather than sex-specific adaptation.
sex and size related spatial distributions of T. nucefera trees in Torreya Forest are not only affected by abiotic heterogeneity but also by stochastic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial pattern of a population is determined by the interaction of multiple factors, such as ecological and evolutionary factors, abiotic factors, and stochastic processes.

the Torreya forest is a mosaic of spatially heterogeneous microhabitats, which are created by Gotjawal terrain, and that this mosaic structure is maintained through complex interactions of ecological, evolutionary, and stochastic processes.
sex and size related patterns are not necessarily correlated with one another in the Torreya forest, suggesting that the role of sex and size in the population is not the same.
